label: conj:cao
title: Conjecture
body_md:
\label{conj:cao}
Let $G$ be a graph with $\chi'(G)=\Delta(G)+k$,
and let $p,q$ be positive integers satisfying $p+q=\Delta(G)+k$ with
$p,q\le\Delta(G)$. Then $G$ can be decomposed into two Class I subgraphs
$H_1$ and $H_2$ such that $\Delta(H_1)=p$ and $\Delta(H_2)=q$.
head: environment
name: Cao et al.\

label: thm:conjecture4.1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:conjecture4.1}
Let $G$ be a finite loopless multigraph with maximum degree $\Delta$ and
$\chi'(G)=\Delta+k$, $k\ge0$. Let $p,q$ be positive integers satisfying
$p+q=\Delta+k$ and $p,q\le\Delta$. Then $G$ has an edge decomposition
$$
E(G)=E(H_p)\mathbin{\dot\cup}E(H_q)
$$
into two spanning Class I subgraphs such that
$$
\Delta(H_p)=p
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\Delta(H_q)=q.
$$
head: environment
name: Main Theorem

label: lem:minclass-rigidity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:minclass-rigidity}
		The set $E_r$ is nonempty. More generally, let $\theta$ be any proper $r$-edge-coloring of $G$ such that $|E_r(\theta)|=|E_r|$, where $E_r(\theta)=\theta^{-1}(r)$, and let $uv\in E_r(\theta)$.
		Then the following hold:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
			\item $\bar{\theta}(u)\cap \bar{\theta}(v)=\varnothing;$
			\item $d_G(u)+d_G(v)\ge r+1;$
			\item for every $\alpha\in \bar{\theta}(u)$ and $\beta\in \bar{\theta}(v)$, the vertices
			$u$ and $v$ are $(\alpha,\beta)$-linked under $\theta$.
		\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that $E_r\ne\varnothing$ since $\chi'(G)=r$.
		
		For (i), suppose that $\alpha\in \bar{\theta}(u)\cap \bar{\theta}(v)$. Since $\theta(uv)=r$, we have $\alpha\ne r$. Recolor $uv$ with $\alpha$. If $|E_r(\theta)|\ge2$, the resulting proper $r$-edge-coloring has a
		color-$r$ class of size $|E_r(\theta)|-1$, contradicting the
		minimality of $|E_r|$. If $|E_r(\theta)|=1$, then we obtain a
		proper $(r-1)$-edge-coloring, contradicting $r=\chi'(G)$. Hence
		$\bar{\theta}(u)\cap \bar{\theta}(v)=\varnothing$.
		
		For (ii), $r\notin \bar{\theta}(u)\cup\bar{\theta}(v)$. By (i), $|\bar{\theta}(u)|+|\bar{\theta}(v)|\le r-1$.
		Since $|\bar{\theta}(u)|=r-d_G(u)$ and $|\bar{\theta}(v)|=r-d_G(v)$,
		we obtain $d_G(u)+d_G(v)\ge r+1$.
		
		For (iii), suppose that $u$ and $v$ are not $(\alpha,\beta)$-linked for some $\alpha\in \bar{\theta}(u)$ and $\beta\in \bar{\theta}(v)$.
		Interchange $\alpha$ and $\beta$ on the $(\alpha,\beta)$-component
		containing $u$. Let $\theta'$ be the resulting proper $r$-edge-coloring. Since $v$ lies in a different component, it is unchanged
		and still misses $\beta$, while $u$ now also misses $\beta$. Since $r\notin\{\alpha, \beta \}$, $E_r(\theta')=E_r(\theta)$. Moreover, $\beta\in \bar{\theta'}(u)\cap\bar{\theta'}(v)$, contrary to (i).
head: environment

label: lem:threshold
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:threshold}
		Let $\psi$ be a proper $r$-edge-coloring of $G$. Suppose vertices $x,y$
		satisfy $\bar{\psi}({x})\cap\bar{\psi}({y})=\varnothing$, $d_G(x)\ge p$ and $d_G(y)\ge q$.
		Then $G$ has an edge decomposition
		$$
		E(G)=E(H_p)\mathbin{\dot\cup}E(H_q)
		$$
		into two spanning Class I subgraphs satisfying
		$$
		\Delta(H_p)=p
		\qquad\text{and}\qquad
		\Delta(H_q)=q.
		$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $X=\bar{\psi}(x)$ and $Y=\bar{\psi}(y)$.
		Since $X\cap Y=\varnothing$, $Y\subseteq[r]\setminus X$.	
		Moreover, $|Y|=r-d_G(y)\le r-q=p$
		and $|[r]\setminus X|=d_G(x)\ge p$.
		Hence there exists $S\subseteq[r]$ such that $Y\subseteq S\subseteq[r]\setminus X$ and $|S|=p$.
		Let $T=[r]\setminus S$.
		Then $|T|=q$.
		
		Let $H_p$ be the spanning subgraph formed by the color classes in $S$, and
		let $H_q$ be the spanning subgraph formed by the color classes in $T$.
		Then
		$$
		E(G)=E(H_p)\mathbin{\dot\cup}E(H_q).
		$$
		Since $H_p$ is the union of $p$ color classes, $\chi'(H_p)\le p$ and $\Delta(H_p)\le p$.
		Because $S\subseteq[r]\setminus X$, every color in $S$ appears at $x$; and so $d_{H_p}(x)=p$.
		Thus
		$$
		\chi'(H_p)=\Delta(H_p)=p.
		$$
		
		Similarly, $Y\subseteq S$ gives $T\cap Y=\varnothing$, so every color in
		$T$ appears at $y$. Hence $d_{H_q}(y)=q$, 
		and therefore
		$$
		\chi'(H_q)=\Delta(H_q)=q.
		$$
head: environment

label: lem:middle
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:middle}
		Let $uv\in E_r$, relabelled so that $d_G(u)\le d_G(v)$. Then
		$$
		p+2\le d_G(u)\le d_G(v)\le q-1.
		$$
		In particular,
		$$
		p\le d_G(u),d_G(v)\le q-1.
		$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since the theorem is assumed false, Lemma~\ref{lem:threshold} cannot apply
		to the endpoints of $uv$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:minclass-rigidity}(i), $\bar{\varphi}(u)\cap \bar{\varphi}(v)=\varnothing$. Hence it is impossible that both
		$$
		d_G(u)\ge p
		\qquad\text{and}\qquad
		d_G(v)\ge q.
		$$
		Therefore $d_G(u)\le p-1$ or $d_G(v)\le q-1$.
		
		By Lemma~\ref{lem:minclass-rigidity}(ii),
		$d_G(u)+d_G(v)\ge r+1=p+q+1.$
		Consequently, exactly one of the following two alternatives holds:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
			\item $$d_G(u)\le p-1,
			\qquad
			d_G(v)\ge q+2;$$
			\item
			$$
			p+2\le d_G(u)\le d_G(v)\le q-1.
			$$
		\end{enumerate}
		It remains to exclude (i).
		
		Suppose, to the contrary, that $d_G(u)\le p-1$ and $d_G(v)\ge q+2$.
		Let $A=\bar{\varphi}(u)$ and $B=\bar{\varphi}(v)$.
		The set $B$ is nonempty because $d_G(v)\le\Delta<r$. Choose $\beta\in B$.
		Since $A\cap B=\varnothing$, $u$ sees $\beta$. Let
		$ux_\beta$ be the unique edge incident with $u$ that is colored $\beta$. Since $v$ misses
		$\beta$, $x_\beta\ne v$.
		
		Fix $\alpha\in A$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:minclass-rigidity}(iii), the vertices
		$u,v$ are $(\alpha,\beta)$-linked. Their common $(\alpha,\beta)$-component is a path joining $u$ and $v$ and contains $ux_\beta$. Since $x_\beta\ne v$, the vertex $x_\beta$ is internal on that path and hence is incident with an edge colored $\alpha$. This holds for every $\alpha\in A$. Therefore
		$$
		d_G(x_\beta)\ge |A|+1=r-d_G(u)+1\ge q+2.
		$$
		
		We claim $\bar{\varphi}(x_\beta)\cap B=\varnothing$.
		Suppose, to the contrary, that there exists $\gamma\in\bar{\varphi}(x_\beta)\cap B$.
		Since $x_\beta$ is incident with an edge colored $\beta$, $\gamma\ne\beta$.
		Choose $\alpha\in A$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:minclass-rigidity}(iii), the
		vertices $u,v$ lie in one $(\alpha,\gamma)$-component, which is a path $P$ joining $u$ and $v$. The vertex $x_\beta$ is incident with an edge colored $\alpha$ and misses $\gamma$, so it has degree one in $G_\varphi(\alpha,\gamma)$. Since $x_\beta\notin\{u,v\}$, it cannot be
		internal on $P$. Thus $x_\beta\notin V(P)$.
		Interchange $\alpha,\gamma$ on $P$. Then $\gamma$ is missing at $u$, while
		$x_\beta$ is unchanged and still misses $\gamma$. Recolor $ux_\beta$ by $\gamma$. 
		Now $\beta$ is missing at $u$, while $v$ still misses $\beta$. Recolor $uv$ by $\beta$.
		The result is a proper $r$-edge-coloring with one fewer edge of color $r$,
		contradicting the minimality of $|E_r|$. Therefore $\bar{\varphi}(x_\beta)\cap B=\varnothing$.
		
		Now
		$$
		d_G(x_\beta)\ge q+2\ge p,
		\qquad
		d_G(v)\ge q+2\ge q,
		$$
		and
		$$
		\bar{\varphi}(x_\beta)\cap\bar{\varphi}(v)=\varnothing.
		$$
		Lemma~\ref{lem:threshold} applies to $x_\beta,v$, a contradiction. Hence (i) is impossible, and (ii) follows.
head: environment

label: lem:blocker-setup
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:blocker-setup}
		Let $\theta$ be a proper $r$-edge-coloring of $G$ satisfying $E_r(\theta)=E_r(\varphi)$, $\bar{\theta}(u)=A$, $\bar{\theta}(v)=B$ and $r\in\bar{\theta}(z)$.
		Then
		$$
		|B\setminus\bar{\theta}(z)|
		\ge
		|A\cap\bar{\theta}(z)|+2.
		$$
		In particular, if $A\cap\bar{\theta}(z)\ne\varnothing$, then $B\setminus\bar{\theta}(z)\ne\varnothing$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $d_G(z)=\Delta$, $|\bar{\theta}(z)|=r-\Delta=k$.
		Moreover, $uv\in E_r(\theta)$, and hence $r\notin A\cup B$.
		By Lemma~\ref{lem:minclass-rigidity}(i), $A\cap B=\varnothing$.
		Since $r\in\bar{\theta}(z)$, it follows that
		$$
		|A\cap\bar{\theta}(z)|
		+
		|B\cap\bar{\theta}(z)|
		\le k-1.
		$$
		
		On the other hand, Lemma~\ref{lem:middle} gives $d_G(v)\le q-1$.
		Therefore $|B|=r-d_G(v)\ge r-(q-1)=p+1\ge k+1$,
		where the last inequality follows from $p\ge k$. Consequently,
		$$
		\begin{aligned}
			|B\setminus\bar{\theta}(z)|
			&=
			|B|-|B\cap\bar{\theta}(z)|\\
			&\ge
			k+1-|B\cap\bar{\theta}(z)|\\
			&\ge
			|A\cap\bar{\theta}(z)|+2.
		\end{aligned}
		$$
head: environment

label: lem:blocker-elimination
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Call a proper $r$-edge-coloring $\theta$ \emph{admissible}
		if $E_r(\theta)=E_r(\varphi)$, $\bar{\theta}(u)=A$, $\bar{\theta}(v)=B$ and $r\in\bar{\theta}(z)$.
		By the definitions of $A$ and $B$ and by the observation above, the coloring $\varphi$ is admissible.
		
		Among all admissible colorings, choose $\theta$ such that $|A\cap\bar\theta(z)|$ is minimum. Suppose, to the contrary, that $A\cap\bar{\theta}(z)\ne\varnothing$. Choose $a\in A\cap\bar{\theta}(z)$.
		By Lemma~\ref{lem:blocker-setup}, there exists $b\in B\setminus\bar{\theta}(z)$.
		
		Since $ \bar{\theta}(u)=A$, $\bar{\theta}(v)=B$ and $A\cap B=\varnothing$, the color $a$ is missing at $u$ and present at $v$, while the color $b$ is missing at $v$ and present at $u$. Moreover, $E_r(\theta)=E_r(\varphi)$ and $uv\in E_r(\theta).$ By Lemma~\ref{lem:minclass-rigidity}(iii), the vertices $u$ and $v$ are $(a,b)$-linked under $\theta$. Hence the $(a,b)$-component containing $u$ and $v$ is a path with endvertices $u$ and $v$.
		
		At $z$, the color $a$ is missing and the color $b$ is present. Thus $z$
		has degree one in $G_\theta(a, b)$. Moreover, $z\notin\{u,v\}$, because $d_G(z)=\Delta$, whereas Lemma~\ref{lem:middle} gives $d_G(u),d_G(v)\le q-1\le\Delta-1$.
		Hence $z$ cannot lie in the $(a,b)$-component containing $u$ and $v$: every non-endvertex of
		that path has degree two in $G_\theta(a, b)$, while $z$ has degree one.
		Thus $P_z(a, b, \theta)$ is distinct from the $(a,b)$-component containing $u$ and $v$.
		
		Interchange $a$ and $b$ on $P_z(a, b, \theta)$, obtaining a proper $r$-edge-coloring $\theta'$. Since $u,v\notin V(P_z(a, b, \theta))$, $\bar{\theta'}(u)=A$ and $\bar{\theta'}(v)=B$.
		Also $a,b\ne r$, because color $r$ is present at both $u$ and $v$.
		Therefore
		$$
		E_r(\theta')=E_r(\theta)=E_r(\varphi).
		$$
		Moreover,
		$$
		\bar{\theta'}({z})
		=
		(\bar{\theta}({z})\setminus\{a\})\cup\{b\}.
		$$
		Since $a\in A$ and $b\in B$ with $A\cap B=\varnothing$,
		$$ |A\cap\bar{\theta'}(z)| = |A\cap\bar{\theta}(z)|-1. $$
		Finally, $a, b\ne r$, so $r$ remains missing at $z$. Hence $\theta'$ is again admissible.
		
		This contradicts the choice of $\theta$. Therefore $A\cap\bar\theta(z)=\varnothing$.
		Taking $\psi=\theta$ completes the proof.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $k=0$, then $\chi'(G)=\Delta$. Let $\varphi$ be a proper
		$\Delta$-edge-coloring of $G$, and choose a vertex $z$ with
		$d_G(z)=\Delta$. Partition the color set $[\Delta]$ into two sets
		$S$ and $T$ with $|S|=p$ and $|T|=q$. Let $H_p$ and $H_q$ be the
		spanning subgraphs formed by the color classes in $S$ and $T$,
		respectively. Since every color in $[\Delta]$ appears at $z$,
		we have
		\[
		d_{H_p}(z)=p
		\qquad\text{and}\qquad
		d_{H_q}(z)=q.
		\]
		Hence
		\[
		\chi'(H_p)=\Delta(H_p)=p,
		\qquad
		\chi'(H_q)=\Delta(H_q)=q.
		\]
		Thus the result holds when $k=0$. Henceforth assume $k\ge1$.
		
		Suppose, to the contrary, that the theorem fails. Choose $\varphi$ and the minimum color class $E_r(\varphi)$ as above, and fix an edge $uv\in E_r(\varphi)$.
		Relabel $u$ and $v$, if necessary, so that $d_G(u)\le d_G(v).$
		By Lemma~\ref{lem:middle}, $p+2\le d_G(u)\le d_G(v)\le q-1$.
		
		Let $A=\bar{\varphi}(u)$, $B=\bar{\varphi}(v)$, and choose a vertex $z$ with $d_G(z)=\Delta$.
		
		By Lemma~\ref{lem:blocker-elimination}, there exists a proper
		$r$-edge-coloring $\psi$ such that
		$$
		\bar{\psi}(u)=A
		$$
		and
		$$
		A\cap\bar{\psi}(z)=\varnothing.
		$$
		Hence
		$$
		\bar{\psi}(u)\cap\bar{\psi}(z)
		=
		A\cap\bar{\psi}(z)
		=
		\varnothing.
		$$
		
		Moreover,
		$$
		d_G(u)\ge p
		$$
		and
		$$
		d_G(z)=\Delta\ge q.
		$$
		Therefore Lemma~\ref{lem:threshold}, applied to $u$ and $z$ under the
		coloring $\psi$, yields an edge decomposition
		$$
		E(G)=E(H_p)\mathbin{\dot\cup}E(H_q)
		$$
		into two spanning Class I subgraphs satisfying
		$$
		\Delta(H_p)=p
		\qquad\text{and}\qquad
		\Delta(H_q)=q.
		$$
		This contradicts the assumption that $G$ is a counterexample.
head: environment
